title: Clio and the Economics of QWERTY
what_it_gives_you: The founding case for lock-in: an early standard survives because everything around it adapts to it. Use it to argue that the divergent system can be permanent even where it is worse.

authors: Liebowitz, S. J.; Margolis, Stephen E.
title: The Fable of the Keys
what_it_gives_you: The rebuttal to David. The QWERTY evidence is thinner than claimed, and markets do switch when an alternative is clearly better. Give this argument to your in-world skeptic, and use it to keep each fork from feeling arbitrary.

title: Competing Technologies, Increasing Returns, and Lock-In by Historical Events
what_it_gives_you: A formal model where small early events plus increasing returns pick the winning technology. Explains how the first few cities to adopt a district system could tip the whole country.

authors: Liebowitz, S. J.; Margolis, Stephen E.
title: Path Dependence, Lock-In, and History
venue: Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization
what_it_gives_you: Sorts path dependence into three degrees by how costly the lock-in is. Use it to decide, story by story, whether their system is worse, equal or better than ours.

title: Nuclear Power Reactors: A Study in Technological Lock-in
what_it_gives_you: Light-water reactors won because the Navy's submarine program got there first. A real case of military procurement choosing a civilian technology.

title: Sprayed to Death: Path Dependence, Lock-in and Pest Control Strategies
what_it_gives_you: Chemical pest control locked in, and some local lock-ins later broke. Useful for a 1970s city where an old district system is starting to crack.

authors: David, Paul A.; Bunn, Julie Ann
title: The Economics of Gateway Technologies and Network Evolution: Lessons from Electricity Supply History
what_it_gives_you: The AC/DC fight and the rotary converter, a gateway device that let rival networks connect. Supports 'compatibility with another technology' as a divergence cause, and the Niagara fork.

title: Path Dependence in Spatial Networks: The Standardization of Railway Track Gauge
what_it_gives_you: How railway gauge standards spread region by region across a network. Explains how a local standard, like a main pressure or a pipe size, radiates out from one city.

title: Understanding Carbon Lock-In
what_it_gives_you: Lock-in happens to technologies and institutions together: utilities, codes, unions, lenders. Populate your 1962-82 city with people whose jobs depend on the divergent system.

title: Technological Transitions as Evolutionary Reconfiguration Processes: A Multi-Level Perspective and a Case-Study
what_it_gives_you: The multi-level perspective: niche, regime and landscape. A simple frame for writing each fork as a niche technology that took over a regime.

title: The Dynamics of Transitions in Socio-Technical Systems: A Multi-Level Analysis of the Transition Pathway from Horse-Drawn Carriages to Automobiles (1860-1930)
what_it_gives_you: The historical horse-to-car transition in US cities, 1860-1930. This is the historical window your Intersection and Meter forks bend.

title: Users as Agents of Technological Change: The Social Construction of the Automobile in the Rural United States
what_it_gives_you: Farmers turned the Model T into a portable power source. Precedent for residents using district systems in ways the engineers never planned.

title: Increasing Returns, Path Dependence, and the Study of Politics
what_it_gives_you: Why political institutions get cheaper to keep and costlier to change over time. Supports municipal politics as a divergence cause.

title: The Art of Standards Wars
what_it_gives_you: The tactics firms use to win standards wars. Useful for the corporate fights at each fork.

authors: Pinch, Trevor J.; Bijker, Wiebe E.
title: The Social Construction of Facts and Artefacts: or How the Sociology of Science and the Sociology of Technology Might Benefit Each Other
what_it_gives_you: Early bicycles had several 'correct' designs depending on who you asked, until the argument closed. Use it to show that in the 1890s their design and ours both looked right to someone.

title: Do Artifacts Have Politics?
what_it_gives_you: Robert Moses's low parkway bridges as design that carries a political decision. A model for an archival artifact that explains why a structure has its shape.

title: Do Politics Have Artefacts?
what_it_gives_you: Shows the Moses bridge story is mostly legend. Pair it with Winner and you have investigators chasing a famous explanation that turns out to be folklore.

title: Technological Momentum in History: Hydrogenation in Germany 1898-1933
what_it_gives_you: Technological momentum: big systems gather people, capital and rules until they are hard to turn. This is why a 1973 resident can't picture the city without its district systems.

title: The Evolution of Large Technological Systems
venue: In Bijker, Hughes and Pinch (eds.), The Social Construction of Technological Systems. MIT Press
what_it_gives_you: System builders, reverse salients and momentum. Vocabulary for the engineers who argued at each fork.

title: The Separate vs. Combined Sewer Problem: A Case Study in Urban Technology Design Choice
what_it_gives_you: A real municipal fork: separate or combined sewers, settled by engineers, cost and doctrine. A template for writing your fork scenes.

title: How the Refrigerator Got Its Hum
venue: In MacKenzie and Wajcman (eds.), The Social Shaping of Technology. Open University Press; reprinted in The Design History Reader, 2nd ed. (Bloomsbury)
what_it_gives_you: Why the compressor refrigerator beat the silent gas-absorption model. Corporate capital and electric utilities decided it. The core source for Cold Room.

title: The Ethnography of Infrastructure
what_it_gives_you: Infrastructure stays invisible until it breaks. This is your series engine: each mystery is a breakdown that makes a system visible.

title: Steps Toward an Ecology of Infrastructure: Design and Access for Large Information Spaces
what_it_gives_you: Infrastructure depends on where you stand: a pipe is invisible to a tenant and central to the crew that maintains it. Use it to vary what each investigator can see.

title: Infrastructure and Modernity: Force, Time, and Social Organization in the History of Sociotechnical Systems
venue: In Misa, Brey and Feenberg (eds.), Modernity and Technology. MIT Press
what_it_gives_you: Mature infrastructures become the natural background of modern life. Backs your rule that the characters never remark on the missing object.

title: The Politics and Poetics of Infrastructure
what_it_gives_you: Infrastructure carries promises and aesthetics along with function. Supports municipal beige as something the city chose on purpose.

title: Out of Order: Understanding Repair and Maintenance
what_it_gives_you: Repair and maintenance as the hidden work that keeps cities running. Most of your protagonists are maintainers.

title: After Innovation, Turn to Maintenance
what_it_gives_you: The case for writing technology history around upkeep. It fits the scratches-and-maintenance-stickers look.

title: From Innovation to Use: Ten Eclectic Theses on the Historiography of Technology
what_it_gives_you: Argues historians should follow technologies in use, long after invention. Your 1962-82 world is exactly that.

title: A Quantitative Approach to the Study of Railroads in American Economic Growth: A Report of Some Preliminary Findings
what_it_gives_you: The famous railroad counterfactual: without railroads, the 1890 US economy comes out only a few percent smaller. A useful constraint, since many forks change daily life far more than they change GDP.

title: What's So Different about a Counterfactual?
what_it_gives_you: How to build counterfactuals that hold up: small rewrites, plausible second-order effects. A checklist for each fork.

title: Why Do We Ask 'What If?' Reflections on the Function of Alternate History
what_it_gives_you: Alternate histories usually work as nightmares or fantasies. Your forks are neither, which helps set the collection apart.

title: Networks of Power: Electrification in Western Society, 1880-1930
what_it_gives_you: The standard history of how electric power systems were built, including the Niagara decision.

authors: Bowker, Geoffrey C.; Star, Susan Leigh
title: Sorting Things Out: Classification and Its Consequences
what_it_gives_you: How classification systems shape what institutions can see. Good for the clerk stories.

title: The Shock of the Old: Technology and Global History since 1900
what_it_gives_you: Old technologies persist and dominate long after the hype. The rationale for your aesthetic.

title: Engineering Rules: Global Standard Setting since 1880
what_it_gives_you: How engineers built the standards bodies that settled forks like these, from 1880 on.

title: Seeing Like a State: How Certain Schemes to Improve the Human Condition Have Failed
what_it_gives_you: Legibility: why states number streets and survey land. Background for The Number.

title: History of Public Works in the United States, 1776-1976
what_it_gives_you: Reference history of American public works. What your municipal agencies would look like.

title: Telling It Like It Wasn't: The Counterfactual Imagination in History and Fiction
what_it_gives_you: Literary history of counterfactual fiction. Helps you place the collection.

title: Counterfactual Thought Experiments in World Politics
what_it_gives_you: Criteria for judging whether a counterfactual is plausible.

title: The Origins and Globalization of Traffic Control Signals
what_it_gives_you: Scholarly history of traffic signals, from London's 1868 semaphore to US electric signals in the 1910s-20s and their spread worldwide.

title: Street Rivals: Jaywalking and the Invention of the Motor Age Street
what_it_gives_you: How motor interests rewrote the rules of the street in the 1920s and turned 'jaywalking' into an offense. A world without signals would have different street law and etiquette.

authors: Lighthill, M. J.; Whitham, G. B.
title: On Kinematic Waves II. A Theory of Traffic Flow on Long Crowded Roads
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A
what_it_gives_you: Kinematic wave theory of traffic. Shows how a disturbance travels backward through traffic and causes crashes at a fixed point far from its cause.

title: Shock Waves on the Highway
what_it_gives_you: An independent derivation of traffic shock waves. Pair with Lighthill and Whitham.

authors: Retting, Richard A.; Persaud, Bhagwant N.; Garder, Per E.; Lord, Dominique
title: Crash and Injury Reduction Following Installation of Roundabouts in the United States
what_it_gives_you: US before-and-after data: converting intersections to modern roundabouts sharply cut injury crashes. Modern roundabouts depend on yield-at-entry and low speed. Older high-speed rotaries had worse records, so your world needs that rule early.

authors: Persaud, Bhagwant N.; Retting, Richard A.; Garder, Per E.; Lord, Dominique
title: Safety Effect of Roundabout Conversions in the United States: Empirical Bayes Observational Before-After Study
what_it_gives_you: The statistical method behind the roundabout safety numbers. Useful if a character has to prove a junction is dangerous with data.

title: Evaluating the Role of Weaving Section Characteristics and Traffic on Crashes in Weaving Areas
what_it_gives_you: Crashes cluster in weaving sections, where entering and exiting traffic cross paths. Grade separation trades crossing conflicts for weaving conflicts, so roads that never cross can still produce collisions.

title: Wrong-Way Driving (Highway Special Investigation Report NTSB/SIR-12/01)
what_it_gives_you: Wrong-way entries onto divided highways, usually through exit ramps. A plausible way for a car to end up on a path it should never be on.

title: The Mechanics of Frost Heaving
what_it_gives_you: How freezing soil lifts structures. One way elevations and clearances drift over decades.

title: A Working Hypothesis for Further Studies of Frost Resistance of Concrete
what_it_gives_you: Why concrete fails under freeze-thaw and how entrained air protects it. Relevant to 1920s-60s concrete in Niagara winters.

title: Expansion of Concrete through Reaction between Cement and Aggregate
venue: Proceedings of the American Society of Civil Engineers
what_it_gives_you: The discovery of alkali-silica reaction: concrete that slowly swells and cracks from within. A mechanism for structures that move.

title: Mechanism and Kinetics of Expansion in the Alkali-Carbonate Rock Reaction
what_it_gives_you: The mechanism of alkali-carbonate expansion in dolomitic aggregate, first identified at Kingston, Ontario, in 1957.

authors: Gillott, J. E.; Swenson, E. G.
title: Mechanism of the Alkali-Carbonate Rock Reaction
what_it_gives_you: Follow-up on the alkali-carbonate mechanism, co-written by Swenson, who first flagged the problem.

authors: Rogers, Chris; Grattan-Bellew, P. E.; Hooton, R. Doug; Ryell, J.; Thomas, M. D. A.
title: Alkali-Aggregate Reactions in Ontario
what_it_gives_you: Survey of alkali-aggregate reaction across Ontario. Key point for you: quarried Niagara Escarpment dolostone is not reactive, so local stone can't be the culprit. Kingston-type aggregate shipped in can.

authors: Galloway, Devin L.; Jones, David R.; Ingebritsen, S. E.
title: Land Subsidence in the United States (USGS Circular 1182)
what_it_gives_you: USGS survey of how land sinks in the US: groundwater pumping, mines, soils. Background for benchmarks that move.

title: Reinforced Concrete and the Modernization of American Building, 1900-1930
what_it_gives_you: How reinforced concrete became standard in American building, 1900-1930. Background for a 'cheap concrete arrives early' fork.

title: Traffic Accident Investigation Manual
what_it_gives_you: The period-standard manual for reconstructing crashes from skid marks, damage and sight lines. What your 1973 investigator actually carries.

title: Indexing the Great Ledger of the Community: Urban House Numbering, City Directories, and the Production of Spatial Legibility
what_it_gives_you: How house numbers and city directories made cities readable to government and business. The system a coordinate address replaces.

title: Governmentality, Geography, and the Geo-Coded World
what_it_gives_you: Geocoding as a tool of government. Frames a coordinate address as a state project with politics attached.

title: Introduction: Governmentality, House Numbering and the Spatial History of the Modern City
what_it_gives_you: Opens a special issue on the history of house numbering across Europe and the US.

authors: Rose-Redwood, Reuben; Alderman, Derek; Azaryahu, Maoz
title: Geographies of Toponymic Inscription: New Directions in Critical Place-Name Studies
what_it_gives_you: Street naming as political inscription. In a coordinate city, who loses the power to name places?

title: House Numbers: Pictures of a Forgotten History
what_it_gives_you: Illustrated history of house numbering since the 18th century.

title: A Comparison of Address Point, Parcel and Street Geocoding Techniques
what_it_gives_you: Street-based address matching can put a point tens of meters off, sometimes much more. Real error sizes for a mislocated address.

title: 'I Think I Discovered a Military Base in the Middle of the Ocean': Null Island, the Most Real of Fictional Places
what_it_gives_you: How blank or broken coordinates collapse to (0, 0) and turn into a real-seeming place in data. A direct model for mail from a coordinate that cannot exist.

title: NADCON: The Application of Minimum-Curvature-Derived Surfaces in the Transformation of Positional Data from the North American Datum of 1927 to the North American Datum of 1983 (NOAA Technical Memorandum NOS NGS-50)
what_it_gives_you: The NGS method for converting NAD 27 coordinates to NAD 83. When a datum changes, every old coordinate lands somewhere slightly new.

title: Evolution of NAD 83 in the United States: Journey from 2D toward 4D
what_it_gives_you: How the NAD 83 datum itself was revised several times. Supports a city whose coordinates quietly move under it.

title: Modernising a Paternoster
venue: 4th Symposium on Lift and Escalator Technologies
what_it_gives_you: Engineering account of modernizing Sheffield's Arts Tower paternoster: 38 cars over 22 occupied floors. A 1970 fatality in Newcastle led UK paternosters to add car-stability tracking. A 2008 survey clocked 60 people per 5-minute peak against 40 for the building's conventional lifts. New paternosters are effectively no longer built.

title: Lifted: A Cultural History of the Elevator
what_it_gives_you: Cultural history of the elevator: how it reorganized buildings, status and privacy.

title: Pedestrian System Planning for High Rise Buildings
what_it_gives_you: Pedestrian flow planning for high-rise buildings, from the Port Authority's research engineer. Numbers for how people queue and board.

authors: Yamaguchi, H.; Osawa, H.; Watanabe, T.; Yamada, H.
title: Brake Control Characteristics of a Linear Synchronous Motor for Ropeless Elevator
venue: Proceedings of the 4th IEEE International Workshop on Advanced Motion Control (AMC '96)
what_it_gives_you: Braking control for a ropeless, linear-motor elevator. Shows where multi-car and continuous-shaft ideas went after the paternoster.

title: The Paternoster: A Requiem
what_it_gives_you: A literary essay on riding paternosters and how it feels like stepping into a building's circulatory system. A tone reference.

authors: Østergaard, Poul Alberg; Werner, Sven; Dyrelund, Anders; Lund, Henrik; et al.
title: The Four Generations of District Cooling: A Categorization of the Development in District Cooling from Origin to Future Prospect
what_it_gives_you: District cooling from the first brine and ammonia pipelines of the late 1800s to today, in four generations. The backbone history for a city that cools by the neighborhood.

authors: Gang, Wenjie; Wang, Shengwei; Xiao, Fu; Gao, Dian-ce
title: District Cooling Systems: Technology Integration, System Optimization, Challenges and Opportunities for Applications
what_it_gives_you: Modern district cooling engineering: plants, networks, storage and failure points. Grounds the physics of a neighborhood cold loop.

title: The Gas Storage of Fruit. II. Optimum Temperatures and Atmospheres
venue: Journal of Pomology and Horticultural Science
what_it_gives_you: Controlled-atmosphere storage: less oxygen and more carbon dioxide slow fruit aging. One lever for food that ages slower than it should.

title: Production of Ethylene by Some Ripening Fruits
what_it_gives_you: The first proof that ripening fruit gives off ethylene.

authors: Burg, Stanley P.; Burg, Ellen A.
title: Role of Ethylene in Fruit Ripening
what_it_gives_you: Ethylene acts as the ripening hormone: tiny concentrations trigger ripening. The main lever for food that ages faster than it should.

authors: Burg, Stanley P.; Stolwijk, J. A. J.
title: A Highly Sensitive Katharometer and Its Application to the Measurement of Ethylene and Other Gases of Biological Importance
venue: Journal of Biochemical and Microbiological Technology and Engineering
what_it_gives_you: A sensitive detector for ethylene built for plant research. Proof that a 1970s investigator could measure ethylene in a cold room.

authors: Ratkowsky, D. A.; Olley, J.; McMeekin, T. A.; Ball, A.
title: Relationship Between Temperature and Growth Rate of Bacterial Cultures
what_it_gives_you: The square-root model linking temperature to bacterial growth rate. Lets you calculate how much a few degrees changes spoilage.

title: A Dynamic Approach to Predicting Bacterial Growth in Food
what_it_gives_you: How to model bacterial growth when temperature changes over time, as it would in a drifting district loop.

title: Application of Chemical Kinetics to Deterioration of Foods
what_it_gives_you: Arrhenius and Q10 kinetics for food deterioration. Rule of thumb: a 10 degree C rise often speeds these reactions 2 to 3 times, so 'radically different rates' needs more than temperature alone.

title: Food Irradiation: Past, Present and Future
what_it_gives_you: History of food irradiation, including the 1950s-60s programs. A darker way food could age slowly in one area.

title: Refrigeration in America: A History of a New Technology and Its Impact
what_it_gives_you: The classic history of American refrigeration, including ice plants and cold storage before the home fridge.

title: Refrigeration Nation: A History of Ice, Appliances, and Enterprise in America
what_it_gives_you: How ice harvesting, ice plants and appliances competed. Good detail on the businesses your fork would change.

title: The Grand Domestic Revolution: A History of Feminist Designs for American Homes, Neighborhoods, and Cities
what_it_gives_you: Kitchenless houses and cooperative housekeeping: the communal path American homes did not take.

title: More Work for Mother: The Ironies of Household Technology from the Open Hearth to the Microwave
what_it_gives_you: Includes the roads not taken in household technology, such as commercial laundries and communal kitchens.

title: When Women Were Switches: Technology, Work, and Gender in the Telephone Industry, 1890-1920
what_it_gives_you: Why the Bell System kept human operators for decades: operators were flexible, cheap and part of the service. The historical basis for operator routing persisting.

title: Universal Service in Telephone History: A Reconstruction
what_it_gives_you: The dual-service era, when many towns ran two unconnected phone networks. A ghost subscriber can live in the seam between systems.

title: Solution of Some Problems in the Theory of Probabilities of Significance in Automatic Telephone Exchanges
venue: Elektroteknikeren (Danish); English translation in Post Office Electrical Engineers' Journal 10:189-197 (1918)
what_it_gives_you: Erlang's formulas for how many operators and lines an exchange needs. Staffing records can reveal traffic the switchboard logs don't show.

title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
venue: Transactions of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers
what_it_gives_you: Relay circuits as Boolean logic. The analysis tool for any electromechanical exchange in your world.

authors: Scudder, F. J.; Reynolds, J. N.
title: Crossbar Dial Telephone Switching System
what_it_gives_you: Bell's crossbar system as introduced. The period machinery that would run alongside operators.

authors: Keister, W.; Ketchledge, R. W.; Vaughan, H. E.
title: No. 1 ESS: System Organization and Objectives
what_it_gives_you: The first electronic switching system. Marks what 1965-75 automation looked like in our history.

title: In-Band Single-Frequency Signaling
what_it_gives_you: In-band single-frequency (2600 Hz) signaling, the weakness phone phreaks later exploited.

title: Signaling Systems for Control of Telephone Switching
what_it_gives_you: Published specifications for multifrequency signaling. How outsiders learned to talk to the network.

title: Appendix E: Reflection Loss Caused by a Bridged Tap
venue: In Subscriber Loop Signaling and Transmission Handbook. IEEE Press / Wiley
what_it_gives_you: Bridged taps: leftover cable branches still connected to a live line. A physical path for a 'disconnected' subscriber to stay on the wire.

title: America Calling: A Social History of the Telephone to 1940
what_it_gives_you: How ordinary people actually used the telephone before 1940.

title: Race on the Line: Gender, Labor, and Technology in the Bell System, 1880-1980
what_it_gives_you: The operator workforce across a century, including how automation reshaped it. Essential for an operator-routed 1970s.

title: Network Nation: Inventing American Telecommunications
what_it_gives_you: How municipal politics shaped telegraph and telephone networks. Strong on the independents versus Bell.

title: Exploding the Phone: The Untold Story of the Teenagers and Outlaws Who Hacked Ma Bell
what_it_gives_you: History of phone phreaking, 1950s-70s. The people who treated the network as a puzzle.

title: Parking Meter (Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History and Culture, entry PA015)
what_it_gives_you: The first parking meter: Oklahoma City, July 16, 1935, with 175 meters on fourteen blocks. The mechanism came from a Tulsa firm that made timers for nitroglycerin oil-well shots.

title: In 1929, an Automatic High-Rise Parking Garage
what_it_gives_you: Kent Automatic Garages, 1929 to the early 1960s. The 25-story garage at 43 West 61st Street held about 1,000 cars moved by an electric 'parker' that hooked the rear axle. A working ancestor of your parking vaults.

authors: Garber, Michael D.; Benmarhnia, Tarik; Mason, Jacob; Morales-Zamora, Emily; et al.
title: Parking and Public Health
what_it_gives_you: Parking's health effects plus a compact history: Los Angeles required off-street parking in 1935, 12% of cities zoned for parking by 1946, and 96% of cities over 25,000 did by 1969.

title: The Trouble with Minimum Parking Requirements
venue: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
what_it_gives_you: Minimum parking requirements reshaped American cities. If municipal vaults replace the parking lot, this paper tells you what land and street life you get back.

authors: Roodbergen, Kees Jan; Vis, Iris F. A.
title: A Survey of Literature on Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems
what_it_gives_you: Survey of automated storage and retrieval: dwell points, storage assignment, relocation. The operating logic of a mechanical parking vault.

title: Automated Stereo-Garage with Multiple Cache Parking Spaces: Structure, System and Scheduling Performance
what_it_gives_you: Scheduling in an automated car garage with cache spaces, where cars get shuffled to speed retrieval. A mechanism for a stored car that 'moves' every day.

authors: Jakle, John A.; Sculle, Keith A.
title: Lots of Parking: Land Use in a Car Culture
what_it_gives_you: History of American parking lots and garages, including mechanical garages.

title: The High Cost of Free Parking
what_it_gives_you: The long-form argument behind Shoup 1999, with the history of parking meters and requirements.

title: Rights Amplification in Master-Keyed Mechanical Locks
what_it_gives_you: Anyone holding one legitimate key to a master-keyed system can work out the master key with a few blanks and some patience. The same logic applies to any hierarchical access system, pneumatic or otherwise.

title: Invisible and Instantaneous: Geographies of Media Infrastructure from Pneumatic Tubes to Fiber Optics
what_it_gives_you: Pneumatic tubes as media infrastructure, and why people treat fast networks as instantaneous. Open access.

title: Opening of the Pneumatic Postal Tube Service in New York City
what_it_gives_you: Contemporary report on New York's pneumatic mail opening in 1897. Period vocabulary and specs.

title: Time-Keeping in Paris
what_it_gives_you: Contemporary account of Paris's pneumatic clock network, which pushed a pulse of air through street mains every minute to move the clock hands.

title: Pipeline as Network: Pneumatic Systems and the Social Order
venue: In Park, Jankowski and Jones (eds.), The Long History of New Media. Peter Lang
what_it_gives_you: Pneumatic systems and the social order they built and enforced.

title: Fluid Amplifiers
what_it_gives_you: The period textbook on fluidic amplifiers: logic built from jets of air or liquid with no moving parts.

title: Fluerics 28: State-of-the-Art 1969 (HDL-TR-1478)
what_it_gives_you: The Army lab that started fluidics in 1959-60 surveys what it could do by 1969. Period-accurate limits and uses for a pneumatic lock.

title: Microfluidic Bubble Logic
what_it_gives_you: Logic with no electronics: bubbles in tiny channels do the computing. Modern proof that fluid logic works.

title: Suspect Identities: A History of Fingerprinting and Criminal Identification
what_it_gives_you: How identification systems were built and trusted. Background for any system that decides who 'is' a resident.

title: Birdsill Holly, Jr. (inductee profile)
what_it_gives_you: Holly founded the Holly Manufacturing Company in Lockport in 1859. After fires in Lockport, he built a system that pumped water through mains to hydrants with no reservoir or standpipe, and over 2,000 cities adopted it. He added district steam heating in 1877. In your world, 'no known reservoir' is normal by design, so the mystery has to be an unlisted pump or intake.

authors: Seck, Momar D.; Evans, David D.
title: Major U.S. Cities Using National Standard Fire Hydrants, One Century After the Great Baltimore Fire (NISTIR 7158)
venue: National Institute of Standards and Technology
what_it_gives_you: In 1904 Baltimore, out-of-town engines could not couple to local hydrants. The push for a national hose thread followed, and a century later many cities still hadn't adopted it. A real compatibility fork.

title: Experiments Relating to Hydraulics of Fire Streams
venue: Transactions of the American Society of Civil Engineers
what_it_gives_you: The foundational fire-stream experiments: how much water, at what pressure, actually reaches a fire.

authors: Scawthorn, C.; O'Rourke, T. D.; Blackburn, F. T.
title: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake and Fire: Enduring Lessons for Fire Protection and Water Supply
what_it_gives_you: San Francisco's 1906 fire and the Auxiliary Water Supply System built after it: high-pressure mains, cisterns and seawater pumping. The closest real version of your district fire mains.

title: Analysis of Flow in Networks of Conduits or Conductors (Engineering Experiment Station Bulletin 286)
what_it_gives_you: The Hardy Cross method for solving flows in looped pipe networks. The standard hand method from 1936 into the computer era, so your investigators would use it.

title: Turbulent Flow in Pipes, with Particular Reference to the Transition Region Between the Smooth and Rough Pipe Laws
venue: Journal of the Institution of Civil Engineers
what_it_gives_you: The friction equation for pipe flow. With Moody's chart, the everyday tool for sizing and diagnosing mains.

title: Friction Factors for Pipe Flow
what_it_gives_you: The Moody chart. Any 1970s water engineer has it on the wall.

authors: Walters, Trey W.; Leishear, Robert A.
title: When the Joukowsky Equation Does Not Predict Maximum Water Hammer Pressures
venue: ASME Pressure Vessels and Piping Conference (PVP2018-84050)
what_it_gives_you: Water hammer: a sudden valve closure sends a pressure spike through a network. Joukowsky's classic estimate, and the cases where real spikes run higher. Also covers the air-main version of the same shock for The Lock.

authors: Puust, R.; Kapelan, Z.; Savic, D. A.; Koppel, T.
title: A Review of Methods for Leakage Management in Pipe Networks
what_it_gives_you: How utilities find leaks and unaccounted-for water: water balances, pressure management, acoustic listening. The detective work of a water system.

title: Isotopic Variations in Meteoric Waters
what_it_gives_you: The global meteoric water line. Evaporated surface water, like a canal or reservoir, plots off the line, so a 1970s lab can tell canal water from groundwater.

title: Continental Water Balance, Ground Water Inventory and Storage Times, Surface Ocean Mixing Rates and World-Wide Water Circulation Patterns from Cosmic-Ray and Bomb Tritium
what_it_gives_you: Bomb-test tritium as a tracer. Water with almost no tritium fell as rain before the 1950s tests, which can date water from a sealed cistern or deep aquifer.

title: The Disaster Experts: Mastering Risk in Modern America
what_it_gives_you: Fire insurance engineers and the rise of safety standards. Insurance standards as a divergence cause.

authors: Piercy, J. E.; Embleton, T. F. W.; Sutherland, L. C.
title: Review of Noise Propagation in the Atmosphere
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_gives_you: How the atmosphere bends and absorbs sound. Temperature inversions and wind gradients carry low-frequency noise far at night.

title: Tutorial on Sound Propagation Outdoors
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_gives_you: Outdoor sound propagation, including ground effects and refraction. The physics of a train heard where it shouldn't be.

authors: Colaço, Aires; Liravi, Hassan; et al.
title: Ground-Borne Vibrations Induced by Railway Traffic: Impact, Prediction, Mitigation and Future Perspectives
what_it_gives_you: Review of railway ground vibration: how train energy moves through soil and rock and comes back up as rumble inside buildings. Open access.

authors: University of Western Ontario; University of Windsor (for Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada)
title: Investigation of the Windsor Hum
what_it_gives_you: A real low-frequency noise traced across an international border to blast-furnace operations on Zug Island. A model investigation for a sound with no visible source.

title: The Hum: An Anomalous Sound Heard Around the World
what_it_gives_you: Survey of 'Hum' reports since the 1970s. Shows how hard low-frequency sources are to locate and how communities react. Published in a fringe-leaning journal, so treat it as a record of reports.

authors: Ogden, Brent D.; Cooper, Chelsey (FHWA and FRA)
title: Highway-Rail Crossing Handbook, Third Edition (FHWA-SA-18-040)
what_it_gives_you: The federal handbook on grade crossings, including the history of crossing elimination. What your world did everywhere, done here case by case.

title: Metropolitan Corridor: Railroads and the American Scene
what_it_gives_you: The railroad landscape of 1880-1930: embankments, cuts, stations, the corridor as a place.

title: On Governors
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London
what_it_gives_you: The first mathematical analysis of feedback governors. A thermostat is a governor, so this is where its theory starts.

title: Rational Psychrometric Formulae: Their Relation to the Problems of Meteorology and of Air Conditioning
what_it_gives_you: Carrier's psychrometric formulas, the base of engineered air conditioning.

authors: Grover, G. M.; Cotter, T. P.; Erickson, G. F.
title: Structures of Very High Thermal Conductance
what_it_gives_you: The heat pipe, invented at Los Alamos: fast, passive heat transport with no pump. Period-accurate hardware for a room held at temperature by something hidden.

title: Theory and Design of Variable Conductance Heat Pipes (NASA CR-2018)
what_it_gives_you: Variable-conductance heat pipes hold a set temperature on their own using a gas reservoir. Spacecraft hardware that keeps a set point with no power and no thermostat.

authors: Zalba, Belén; Marín, José M.; Cabeza, Luisa F.; Mehling, Harald
title: Review on Thermal Energy Storage with Phase Change: Materials, Heat Transfer Analysis and Applications
what_it_gives_you: Phase-change materials soak up and release heat at a fixed melting point. A large mass that melts near 20 degrees C (68 degrees F) pins a room near that temperature.

title: Thermal Storage in Salt-Hydrates
venue: In Murr (ed.), Solar Materials Science. Academic Press
what_it_gives_you: Salt-hydrate heat storage from Maria Telkes, who built the 1948 Dover Sun House around it.

title: Air-Conditioning America: Engineers and the Controlled Environment, 1900-1960
what_it_gives_you: Engineers wanted whole-building 'manufactured weather'; consumers bought window units. The exact fork The Dial bends.

title: Explaining the Spread of Residential Air Conditioning, 1955-1980
what_it_gives_you: Why home air conditioning spread from 1955 to 1980: incomes, prices, climate. The spread your world routes through district systems.

title: The End of the Long Hot Summer: The Air Conditioner and Southern Culture
what_it_gives_you: How air conditioning remade the South. With district climate in place of window units, some of that shift weakens.

title: The Rise of the Sunbelt
what_it_gives_you: Argues Sunbelt growth owed more to housing supply and productivity than to air conditioning. Keeps the 'AC built the Sunbelt' claim honest.

authors: Barreca, Alan; Clay, Karen; Deschenes, Olivier; Greenstone, Michael; Shapiro, Joseph S.
title: Adapting to Climate Change: The Remarkable Decline in the US Temperature-Mortality Relationship over the Twentieth Century
what_it_gives_you: Air conditioning drove the fall in US heat deaths after 1960. A district-climate world needs its own version of that health story.

authors: Lund, Henrik; Werner, Sven; Wiltshire, Robin; Svendsen, Svend; et al.
title: 4th Generation District Heating (4GDH): Integrating Smart Thermal Grids into Future Sustainable Energy Systems
what_it_gives_you: The four generations of district heating, from steam to low-temperature networks. Tells you which generation your 1970s city runs.

title: International Review of District Heating and Cooling
what_it_gives_you: Where district heating and cooling won worldwide, and why.

title: Address to the Nation About Policies To Deal With the Energy Shortages (November 7, 1973)
what_it_gives_you: Nixon asked Americans to turn thermostats down at least 6 degrees for a national daytime average of 68 degrees F. Your 68 degrees has a date.

authors: Koenig, W.; Dunn, H. K.; Lacy, L. Y.
title: The Sound Spectrograph
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_gives_you: Bell Labs' sound spectrograph: a picture of sound over time. Lets an investigator read a train's wheel rhythm or a machine's hum off paper.

authors: James, A. T.; Martin, A. J. P.
title: Gas-Liquid Partition Chromatography: The Separation and Micro-Estimation of Volatile Fatty Acids from Formic Acid to Dodecanoic Acid
what_it_gives_you: The founding paper of gas chromatography. By the 1960s, GC identifies gases, solvents and fuels in routine labs.

authors: Fellegi, Ivan P.; Sunter, Alan B.
title: A Theory for Record Linkage
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
what_it_gives_you: The statistical theory for matching records across databases that share no clean key. Exactly the work of a clerk reconciling two city databases, and the way a false match creates a person who never existed.

authors: Newcombe, H. B.; Kennedy, J. M.; Axford, S. J.; James, A. P.
title: Automatic Linkage of Vital Records
what_it_gives_you: Early computer linkage of birth and marriage records. Evidence that probabilistic matching was already in use by 1959.

authors: Jeffreys, A. J.; Wilson, V.; Thein, S. L.
title: Individual-Specific 'Fingerprints' of Human DNA
what_it_gives_you: Boundary marker: DNA fingerprinting arrives in 1985, after your window. A 1962-82 story can't use it.

title: The Road to Lockport: Historical Background of District Heating and Cooling
what_it_gives_you: Birdsill Holly installed the first successful commercial district heating system in Lockport in 1877; more than 50 existed by 1890, and district cooling with brine and ammonia followed. The historical anchor for putting the collection in Lockport.

title: The International Niagara Commission of 1891
venue: In Driven by Demand: How Energy Gets Its Power. Cambridge University Press
what_it_gives_you: The 1890-91 commission that judged how to send Niagara's power to Buffalo. The documented decision point your energy fork bends.

title: Transmitting the Power of Niagara: Scientific, Technological, and Cultural Contexts of an Engineering Decision
what_it_gives_you: Argues the Niagara choice rested on cultural assumptions as much as engineering. Good material for engineers arguing at your fork.

title: Energy in Niagara Falls: International Niagara Commission [History]
what_it_gives_you: IEEE history of the commission and its competition entries.

title: A Review of the Case for Modern-Day Adoption of Hydraulic Air Compressors
what_it_gives_you: Review of hydraulic air compressors, trompe-style machines that make compressed air from falling water with almost no moving parts. The Ragged Chutes plant in Ontario ran on this principle from 1910 for about 70 years.

title: Love Canal: A Toxic History from Colonial Times to the Present
what_it_gives_you: Includes William T. Love's canal and Model City plan of the 1890s, and how the unfinished ditch became Love Canal.
